objective.statement: Recognise and build the tonic triad of C, G, D and F major.
successCriteria: I know a triad is three notes: degrees 1, 3 and 5 of the scale.
I know the tonic triad is built on degree 1, with the root at the bottom.
I can write and recognise the tonic triad in the four Grade 1 keys.

explanation.text: A triad is a chord of three notes, built by taking every other note of the scale: degree 1, degree 3 and degree 5. The tonic triad starts on the tonic, degree 1.

music.textAlternative: A treble stave with the tonic triad of C major: C, E and G sounded together.

explanation.caption: The tonic triad of C major: C (1), E (3) and G (5).

explanation.text: When the root, the note the triad is named after, is the lowest note, the triad is in root position. In this course all triads are in root position.

music.textAlternative: A treble stave with the tonic triad of G major: G, B and D sounded together.

explanation.caption: The tonic triad of G major: G, B and D. All three are in the key without any change.

music.textAlternative: A treble stave with the tonic triad of D major: D, F sharp and A.

explanation.caption: The tonic triad of D major: D, F♯ and A. The 3rd, F♯, comes from the major scale, so it needs a sharp.

explanation.text: Take the scale, then every other note: skip a note, take a note, skip a note, take a note.

music.textAlternative: The notes of the C major tonic triad one after the other: C, E and G, each linked to its key.

steps: Tap C, then E, then G, one at a time. These are degrees 1, 3 and 5.
On the keyboard, notice they are every other white key: C, skip D, E, skip F, G.
Played together they make the tonic triad of C major.
demonstration.textAlternative: Notes C, E and G one after another, showing every other note of the C major scale.

guided.prompt: Part of the tonic triad of D major is shown. Which note is missing from the chord?

music.textAlternative: A bass-clef stave with two notes sounded together: D and F♯.

hints: The tonic triad is degrees 1, 3 and 5 of the scale.

mistakes.wrong-degree: Find the root: rearrange the notes into stacked 3rds — the lowest note of that stack is the root.
mistakes.root-confused-with-bass: The lowest note isn't always the root. Stack the notes in 3rds to find it, then check the inversion.
mistakes.inversion-misread: Inversion depends on which note of the triad is in the bass: root (a), 3rd (b) or 5th (c).
mistakes.leading-note-not-raised: In minor keys, chords use the harmonic minor, so the leading note is raised.
mistakes.note-missing: One of the notes doesn't belong. A triad has a root, a 3rd and a 5th.

feedback.fallback: Not quite. Find the root first, then the bass note.

w1.reason: A triad is built from the tonic, the note two steps above it (the 3rd) and the note four steps above it (the 5th).

w2.reason: The top note of a triad is the 5th of the scale, not the 4th.
